site_surface.short_summary: A loose red-green alliance of Ravnican clans rooted in ruined spaces, lost wild places, Rubblebelt territory, and direct resistance to imposed civilization.
site_surface.one_sentence_identity: The Gruul Clans are Ravnica?s red-green clans of dispossessed wildness, clan autonomy, direct action, and anti-civilization grievance.
site_surface.tagline: Wild places lost. The clans answer directly.
best_for: users who distrust systems that erase living places
users drawn to direct action and local belonging
users who value wildness with territory, clan, or ecological context
content_warnings_or_sensitivity_notes: Gruul lore includes violence, raids, oppression, enslavement, body scarring, and destructive anti-civilization themes.

core_identity.summary: The Gruul Clans are a loose red-green Ravnican guild of clans whose source-bounded identity combines lost stewardship of wild places, Rubblebelt and ruined-space territory, direct action, strength-tested leadership, and anti-civilization grievance.
unknowns: Current long-term post-War-of-the-Spark Gruul leadership was not established by the reviewed official sources.
core_identity.philosophy: Gruul freedom is not generic impulse; it is clan and wildness answering what urban expansion took from them.
core_identity.central_tension: Gruul is strongest when rage protects territory, memory, clan, or wildness, and weakest when flattened into random rage, generic aggression, or mindless destruction.

structure.summary: Gruul organization is loose and clan-based rather than bureaucratic. Gatecrash-era material identifies several stable clans and emphasizes that no leader had fully unified all Gruul clans. Ravnica Allegiance-era material says the clan count changes over time, that seven clans existed then, and that many Gruul follow whoever appears strongest at the moment.

known_roles.description: Leadership is clan-centered and strongly tied to perceived strength, combat reputation, and the ability to command fear, awe, or loyalty.
Gruul history and certain clans, especially Zhur-Taa, preserve shamanic and druidic connections to beasts, old ways, and deep-earth religious expectations.
Official sources repeatedly associate Gruul with raiding parties, warfare, assaults, riot, and direct combat.
Story evidence shows Ghor chieftain authority being challenged publicly and Zhur-Taa war-party selection being performed through a leader touching upheld weapons.
Story evidence adds Gruul shamans as scouts, magic-users, and figures associated with clan leadership or destructive reputation, including Kal, Nikya, and Baas.
The Ghor Clan story uses tattooing, territory maps, and shining ink as a way to carry clan memory, rage, and destroyed-place identity.

leaders.role: Burning Tree clan leader; Gruul de facto leader / mightiest clan leader in relevant eras
leaders.notes: Gatecrash-era sources emphasize that he had not unified all clans; later sources state Domri bested and replaced him.

leaders.role: Planeswalker; Gruul leader / guildmaster during the Ravnica Allegiance and War of the Spark period
leaders.notes: Domri died during War of the Spark after his Spark was harvested by an Eternal.

leaders.name: Ruric Thar
leaders.notes: The name represents a two-headed ogre leader in official Gatecrash-era material.

leaders.name: Nikya of the Old Ways
leaders.role: Leader of the Zhur-Taa clan; shaman

locations.name: The Rubblebelt
locations.relationship_to_faction: Primary Gruul-associated territory and recurring conflict zone with civilization and encroaching guilds.
locations.notes: Described as discontinuous and bordered or surrounded by more civilized areas.

locations.name: Skarrg
locations.relationship_to_faction: Traditional place where Gruul clans periodically converge without guaranteed truce.
locations.notes: Associated with bonfires, roasted giant boars, battles, and temporary camaraderie.

locations.name: The Husk
locations.relationship_to_faction: Home ground of the Slizt clan.
locations.notes: Known for elevated ruins used by Slizt ambushers.

locations.name: Tenth District outskirts
locations.relationship_to_faction: A Gruul encampment is described as steadily encroaching into a neighborhood at the outskirts of the Tenth District.

locations.name: Rubblebelt-adjacent hidden bunker
locations.relationship_to_faction: A bunker near the Gruul Rubblebelt is hidden by weeds and cindervine enchantments and includes baby hydras.
locations.notes: Story-specific location texture from Clans & Legions.

locations.name: Zhur-Taa territory
locations.relationship_to_faction: Zhur-Taa territory is the site of Kal’s surveillance of Izzet activity and Nikya’s bloodcrime response in Gruul Ingenuity.

internal_divisions.name: Burning Tree clan
internal_divisions.description: Largest, most diverse, and most powerful stable Gruul clan in the Gatecrash-era guide; associated with Borborygmos and with a symbol widely treated as the guild symbol.
internal_divisions.notes: Later clan count changed, but Burning Tree remains central to reviewed sources.

internal_divisions.name: Ghor clan
internal_divisions.description: Clan led by Ruric Thar and described as responsible for especially frequent and savage assaults on Ravnican citizenry.
internal_divisions.notes: Also appears in 'Rage of the Unsung' as a story context.

internal_divisions.name: Scab clan
internal_divisions.description: Multi-race clan whose warriors despise pretentiousness and treat scarred or maimed bodies as authentic outward expressions of spirit.

internal_divisions.name: Bolrac clan
internal_divisions.description: Clan of large brutes whose leadership changes frequently and whose members specialize in toppling large structures.

internal_divisions.name: Slizt clan
internal_divisions.description: Mostly viashino clan using stealth, elevation, ranged attacks, and ambush tactics from high ruins.

internal_divisions.name: Zhur-Taa clan
internal_divisions.description: Old-ways clan tied to beasts, shamans, the Utmungr, and expectation of a boar-god apocalypse.
internal_divisions.notes: Gatecrash and Ravnica Allegiance sources both support its mythic/religious importance.

unknowns: Reviewed sources did not identify every one of the seven Ravnica Allegiance-era clans by name.
Reviewed sources did not establish a stable post-Domri long-term Gruul leader.

great_tension.summary: Gruul?s central tension is erased wildness versus totalizing city, not chaos versus order in the abstract. Official sources support former wild-place stewardship, anti-civilization pressure, loose clan belonging, and direct action; story-localized evidence adds territorial and memory-preserving anger without turning every Gruul signal into random destruction.
great_tension.interpretation_warning: The ecological/grievance framing is source-supported, but the exact wording of this tension is interpretive synthesis.

historical_timeline.event: Before the guilds, Gruul druids and shamans celebrated and claimed the wilds of Ravnica.
When the Guildpact was written, the Gruul were given stewardship over Ravnica's wild places and natural beauty.
Urban expansion and other guilds' disregard for Gruul warnings destroyed wilderness and contributed to Gruul marginalization and enslavement.
historical_timeline.notes: This is the official flavor guide's historical framing.

historical_timeline.event: Gruul leadership crumbled and the Gruul became agents of chaos and destruction.
historical_timeline.date_or_era: After centuries of marginalization and oppression

historical_timeline.event: Gatecrash-era sources described six stable Gruul clans and Borborygmos as the mightiest clan leader.
historical_timeline.notes: Later sources say clan count changes and identify seven clans during Ravnica Allegiance.

historical_timeline.event: Zhur-Taa claim bloodcrime and hunt Rakdos after a reported massacre and territorial defilement in Gruul Ingenuity.
historical_timeline.notes: Story-supported; Rakdos blame is presented through in-world characters.

historical_timeline.event: Arrus challenges Ruric and Thar over the dying Rubblebelt, leading them to answer that Selesnya will get war in Rage of the Unsung.
historical_timeline.notes: Key story event for protective/ecological Rage interpretation.

historical_timeline.event: Boros/Wojek material in Clans & Legions ties Baas Solvar Radley, a Gruul prisoner-release request, and a Gruul encampment near the Tenth District.
historical_timeline.date_or_era: Guilds of Ravnica story era / published 2018-10-24
historical_timeline.notes: Boros-file perspective; useful for relationship and location metadata.

key_figures.role: Cyclops; Burning Tree leader; de facto / mightiest Gruul leader in relevant eras
key_figures.relationship_to_faction: A central strength-based leader whose authority derived from personal might and Burning Tree's dominance.
key_figures.notes: Supplanted by Domri in Ravnica Allegiance / War of the Spark-era sources.

key_figures.role: Planeswalker; Gruul leader / guildmaster during a short era

key_figures.name: Ruric Thar
key_figures.relationship_to_faction: Represents one of the major clan leadership structures within Gruul.
key_figures.notes: Official guide identifies Ruric Thar as a two-headed ogre.

key_figures.name: Nikya of the Old Ways
key_figures.relationship_to_faction: Embodies the old-ways, shamanic, deep-earth side of Gruul culture.

key_figures.name: Gan Shokta
key_figures.relationship_to_faction: Appears among Gruul fighters in War of the Spark.
key_figures.notes: Included as a story appearance, not a structural leader in the reviewed sources.

key_figures.name: Kal
key_figures.relationship_to_faction: Serves Nikya’s Zhur-Taa assignment and demonstrates improvisational magic in Gruul Ingenuity.
key_figures.notes: Useful for placement nuance; not treated as a major cross-story character.

key_figures.name: Arrus
key_figures.role: Ghor Clan viashino tattoo artist and challenger
key_figures.relationship_to_faction: POV character for Ghor Rage, clanless exile, Rubblebelt decline, and the public challenge to Ruric and Thar.

key_figures.name: Dryzek
key_figures.relationship_to_faction: His return from prison creates a power-struggle test for Ghor Clan loyalty and chieftain authority.

key_figures.name: Baas Solvar Radley
key_figures.relationship_to_faction: Boros-file material identifies Baas Solvar Radley, while Gruul story material recognizes Baas as a shaman with destructive reputation.
key_figures.notes: Use full name for Clans & Legions; avoid assuming details beyond inspected sources.

canonical_flavor_text.short_excerpt_or_summary: The city took the wild; the clans answer from the rubble.
canonical_flavor_text.notes: Project synthesis for display flavor only; not an exact card quote and not supported by discovery-only story-corpus rows.

views_on_other_factions.relationship_summary: Other guilds' encroachment on Gruul-occupied Rubblebelt territory generates recurring conflict.
views_on_other_factions.notes: Keep broad; do not invent specific bilateral politics without source support.

views_on_other_factions.relationship_summary: Official story evidence shows at least one Gruul narrator identifying anger at Selesnya as part of his Rage, while also acknowledging Selesnyan healing magic as nature-kindred but orderly. Story evidence adds Arrus’s conclusion that Selesnya growth magic leaches Gruul land and Ruric-and-Thar’s answer of war.
views_on_other_factions.notes: Based on a character-perspective story; avoid overgeneralizing to all Gruul.

views_on_other_factions.relationship_summary: Gruul identity is repeatedly framed around hostility to civilization and the desire for the natural world to reclaim Ravnica.
views_on_other_factions.notes: This is a broader civilizational stance rather than a single guild-to-guild relationship.

views_on_other_factions.relationship_summary: In Gruul Ingenuity, Zhur-Taa characters blame Rakdos for a massacre and assemble a hunt in response.
In Gruul Ingenuity, Kal watches Izzet activity near Zhur-Taa territory and later adapts observed Izzet-like fire and lightning into an act Durri accepts as feeling Gruul.
In Clans & Legions, Boros/Wojek material involves Gruul prisoner-release logistics, Gruul riot records, and a Gruul encampment near the Tenth District.

mechanics.summary: Riot and bloodrush are the source-backed Gruul mechanics expression: riot turns immediacy into a choice between haste and added force, while bloodrush turns a creature card in hand into direct combat pressure for an attacking creature. Use these mechanics to reinforce Gruul's dispossession, wildness, clan pressure, and direct action; do not promote unrelated search metadata terms as Gruul mechanics without a future approved source pass.

entries.associated_set: Ravnica Allegiance; Ravnica Remastered reprint/rules support
entries.rules_summary: A creature with riot enters with its controller's choice of a +1/+1 counter or haste. The choice is made as the creature enters the battlefield and cannot be responded to as a separate choice.
entries.design_or_flavor_connection: Riot turns Gruul immediacy into a gameplay fork: hit faster or hit bigger.
entries.notes: Use current Comprehensive Rules for future rules-critical updates.

entries.rules_summary: Bloodrush is an ability word for activated abilities on creature cards in hand; the player pays a cost and discards the card to target an attacking creature with a card-specific combat bonus.
entries.design_or_flavor_connection: Bloodrush supports a combat-first Gruul pattern: a creature can become immediate force even before being cast.
